I am 68 and only started farming last year, so honestly I am still learning. I watch what my neighbor Old Chen does and I ask the young man at the seed supply shop in town. I do not know fancy techniques. I just want to make sure the land produces enough to cover our costs and have some left over. There are only two of us at home, so labor is tight — my back is not what it was.

My land is 10.1 mu. The wheat and maize rotate on the same 6 mu, and I keep 4.1 mu separate for cotton. The cotton brings cash, so I keep it even though it is hard work.

For **wheat**, I will plant in October what the seed shop tells me is a good local variety — probably Kenong 199 or similar. I will rotary-till before planting. I will apply fertilizer in one base dressing and one topdressing at jointing. I will irrigate four times: before winter, at jointing, heading, and grain fill. I have well water so this I can do.

For **maize**, I plant straight after wheat harvest in June. I will not till again — the soil is soft enough and I am tired from wheat harvest. I will use a hybrid seed because I heard it yields more. I will put fertilizer down at planting and again at the big-bell stage.

For **cotton**, I will rotary-till in spring, plant in late April. Cotton needs more spraying — worms and aphids are bad. I will spray when I see trouble, probably five times. I will irrigate more carefully because cotton doesn't like waterlogging but needs water at flowering and boll set.

I am not trying to be scientific. I am trying not to make mistakes in my second year.
